BACKWARDS COMPATIBLE - Service providers want to offer upgrades as options, not total reinstallations. This makes backwards compatible systems highly desirable. Frame Relay is an excellent example of this concept. Frame Relay is a network service that can be implemented using existing links...
Wideband: Digital telecom up to 45 Mbps (T - 3) or 34 Mbps (E - 3)
Narrowband: Digital telecom up to 1.544 Mbps (T - 1) or 2.048 Mbps (E - 1)
Baseband: Analog audio (0 - 20 kHz) and video (0 - 4.2 MHz)
DEFINITION
BANDWIDTH - Defined by capacity: Baseband: Analog audio

BANDWIDTH DISTANCE PRODUCT - Used by fiber optic network designers exclusively to determine the type of cable needed to make a link. If the link is analog, like plain old telephone service (POTS), the bandwidth is in hertz. For example, 16 kHz bandwidth X 30 miles equals 480 kHz miles. In digital, bits per second are used. 1.544 Mbps X 20 miles equals 20.88 Mbps miles. Fiber products are often listed in Mbps kilometers, so mile to km conversion is required.
DEFINITION
DEFINITION

BIT ERROR RATE (BER) - Expressed in powers of 10, a BER of 10 means that 1 bit in 1 billion has to be retransmitted or is lost. BER is measured by special instruments and/or built-in test equipment. The BER requirement is dependent on the type of service provided by a telecom circuit..
DEFINITION

BIT RATE - If you divide the bit rate by 10, this is the approximate amount of overhead bits that is transmitted with the data characters. For example, if you need 10 Mbps of data over a link, ask for at least 11 to 12 Mbps. Overhead is a function of addressing and routing in digital systems. Another factor is retransmission, which also knocks down overall bit rate.
DEFINITION

CLICKTHROUGH RATE - Applies to e-commerce (electronic commerce). Clickthrough is a measure of Internet advertising. If your web page, website, banner, or address has a clickthrough rate of 50%, it means half of the web surfers that access the domain click on your virtual address...
DEFINITION

LATENCY - The amount of time it takes to get information through a telecom network. For example, plain old telephone service has a latency of 400 milliseconds. Latency is caused by propagation delay, transmission delay, processing delay, and/or rotation delay...
DEFINITION

QUALITY OF SERVICE (QoS) - Subjective quality measurement scale. In Asynchronous Transfer Mode (ATM), QoS is somewhat standardized. The objective is 100% QoS; 99.999% (five 9s) is often acceptable. There are 4 classes of ATM service based on QoS: * Class 1: Digital telephone lines * Class 2: Multimedia * Class 3: Data networks * Class 4: Internettt
DEFINITION
SIGNAL-TO-NOISE RATIO - One of the oldest quality
DEFINITION

SPECTRUM EFFICIENCY - Microwave radio quality standard. For digital systems, the efficiency rating is expressed in bits per hertz. For example, a 30 GHz microwave link can move 40 Mbps over a 100 MHz spectrum (29.9 to 30.1 GHz). The spectrum efficiency would be 40/100 = 0.4. If the link were analog, the efficiency is expressed in kHz per channel...

ASYNCHRONOUS TRANSFER MODE (ATM) - Conventional networks carry information in a synchronous manner; empty and full segments are continuously transmitted. ATM is asynchronous (not synchronous) because there are no fixed time slots and empty segments are not transmitted. ATM operates one of 3 bit rates: 25.6 Mbps, 155.52 Mbps, or 622.08 Mbps....
DEFINITION

CABLE - An overall encompassing term for service brought to the consumer on other than twisted pair wire. Common configuration is single conductor with shield (coax). Cable television and digital subscriber services are the most readily recognized services...
DEFINITION

COMMON CARRIERS - Companies required to provide communications services by law (e.g. AT&T). Common Carriers are licensed by the FCC or other regulatory body if outside the US. Other Common Carriers (OCC) provide long distance services at lower cost...
DEFINITION

CLEC - Often pronounced see-leck, these companies came on the scene after the Telecom Act of 1996. CLECs operate their own local loops or lease the lines from the ILECs (Incumbent Local Exchange Carriers). Cellular/wireless providers are the most recognizable CLECs...
DEFINITION
DSL (Digital Subscriber Line) - Digital information on wired twisted pair technology. There are about 20 different types of DSL. DSL bit rates are advertised upwards of 8 Mbps.
DEFINITION

FRAME RELAY - Virtual networking process offered by telecom service providers. Frame Relay works well in wide area networks (WAN) that use a variety of transmission formats. Compatibility with widely different technologies is Frame Relay's most popular feature.ture.
DEFINITION

ISDN - Telephone line high-speed data transfer service. Originated in 1979, ISDN is still popular because a single phone line can be used to connect to the Internet, fax, and voice at the same time. An ISDN BRI (Basic Rate Interface) line carries voice and data...
DEFINITION

PCS (Personal Communications Service) - 1900 MHz range digital wireless telephone service. Conventional cellular telephone operates in the 800 to 900 MHz range. PCS sound quality is known to be better than cellular phone...
DEFINITION

SONET - Fiber optic cables carry enormous volumes of data because of SONET technology. SONET is strictly a broadband transport system. CLECs use SONET for network construction almost exclusively. SONET may eventually replace twisted pair copper...
DEFINITION

T CARRIER - A four-wire system, one pair transmits and one pair receives. A T1 line carries 24 telephone lines. T2 is 4 times T1 (96 phone lines). T3 is 28 T1s. T1 has become a standard for digital data also. If a customer wants a T1, 1.544 Mbps is the desired data rate...

EIA - Organized into several industrial divisions, one of which is the telecom division (TIA). One of the most important standards to be issued by the organization is EIA/TIA 568 - Commercial Building Wiring Standard for Telecom...

ETSI - A standards body with over 900 members from 54 countries. The organization is customer oriented and provides excellent support via their website.

FCC USOC - Software development language and the basis of all telephone service in the US. New companies use the USOC, although it may be called something else. All telephone records, customer service agreements, and technical information is in USOC format. USOC has been in use since around 1984...

IEEE - One of the world's largest trade organizations. IEEE 802 is recognized as the local area network standard. A relatively new product standard is IEEE 1394, popularly called FireWire.
DEFINITION

ISO - The world's leading quality organization. ISO 9000 is a series of standards that outlines a quality program for organizations, included are research & development procedures, manufacturing & installation, and testing & final inspection. Although not telecom specific, ISO certification is essential for telecom companies from a business perspective...
DEFINITION

ITU - The most influential organization in the telecom industry. ITU standards cover every aspect of telecom. The organization originated in 1865 as Union Telegraphique. By 1947, the ITU had evolved into the current organizational structure. P.139 is the standard for USB (Universal Serial Bus) when used as a link. X.400 is the standard for e-mail (electronic mail) exchange.
DEFINITION

TIA 607 - Grounding and bonding standards
TIA PN-2416 - Backbone cabling for residential and commercial buildings...s

WTO - Resolves trade disputes between member countries. Common carrier to common carrier conflicts are frequent. International telecom is a reality because of the WTO.

ENCAPSULATING BRIDGE - A device that connects 2 networks together using data packet encapsulation. For example, an ethernet packet is transported into an ATM network through encapsulation. The original ethernet packet is placed in an ATM envelope so the receiving network can use the data in the packet...

GARAGE BAND - Unlicensed frequency bands or ISM (Industrial, Scientific, Medical) as identified by the FCC. Traditionally garage band radios were used for in-building applications like wireless LANs, bar code readers, and surveillance systems. Since the frequencies are unlicensed, mutual interference can result.....

FIBER PIGTAILS - Used on the source package. Light Emitting Diode (LED) fiber optic sources may be ordered in pigtailed or unpigtailed configuration. Pigtails couple the light from the source to the medium. This technique resolves inherent alignment problems. --
DEFINITION

GSM - Often misinterpreted as Global System for Mobile, when it actually means Special Mobile Group (in English). GSM is an ETSI standard. GSM is a world-renowned mobile communications system. The standard is highly adaptable for cellular phone Internet connectivity (Web Phone)...
DEFINITION

INTELSAT - Consortium owned by a number of governments. INTELSAT is often misinterpreted. The first connotation is usually intelligence satellite. In fact, INTELSAT owns more than 20 of its own satellites. Public services include international, regional, and local telephone. Business services like teleconferencing and data transmission are also offered.
DEFINITION

JUMPERS - Wires installed in make or break circuits. Another form of the jumper is the loopback. Loopbacks are plugs designed to interconnect circuits. A common loopback type is used in T carrier lines where the Tx pair and Rx pair are connected together...
DEFINITION

MA BELL - Some people still refer to common carriers in the US as Ma Bell. Pa Bell was never used. The term Ma Bell will live as long as there are people who remember the old Bell System. The original Bell organization was dismantled with the divesture of AT&T in 1984...
DEFINITION
OPEN SYSTEMS INTERCONNECTION MODEL - The OSI model is the standard for network protocol design. The concept of interconnect layers is used to establish a paradigm and common language...

PBX - P is for private, which means the PBX is switchgear that you can own. A PBX is like a central office where the owner controls trunk lines, dialing, and system architecture. If a business has telecom needs, the PBX is one of the solutions. Recently, the PBX is being adapted to meet Voice over Internet Protocol (Voice over IP) services.

RAIN FADE - Rain is the enemy of microwave. The perfect world for microwave is a vacuum with no rain. Satellite is also subject to rain fade. The water droplets absorb RF energy and attenuate the transmitted signal. This effect is usually negated by increasing output power...
DEFINITION

SMOKEWARE - Also called vaporware, is developed by highly motivated business people. Since Smokeware is only a dream or at best a prototype, it is usually not ready for issue on the date promised. Without Smokeware, telecom technology would stagnate...
DEFINITION

MODULAR PHONE JACKS - Called RJ (Registered Jack), these items are available in a number of configurations. RJ-45, 8 pins with 8 wires, is used for data comm. RJ-11, 6 pins with 4 wires, is the most common telephone jack in the world. There are several other configurations, but the terms RJ-45 and
RJ-11 are universally accepted. Technically, a standard telephone jack is an RJ-14.

MODULAR PHONE JACKS - Called RJ (Registered Jack), these items are avail. in a number of configurations. RJ-45, 8 pins with 8 wires, is used for data comm. RJ-11, 6 pins with 4 wires, is the most common telephone jack in the world. There are several other configurations, but the terms RJ-45 and RJ-11 are universally accepted. Technically, a standard telephone jack is an RJ-14.
DEFINITION

UTP - An interface technology and protocol. By twisting 2 wires together, crosstalk from adjacent wires is minimum and signal strength can be maximum to cover a greater distance. The pairs of wires are also stronger because there is more copper metal and plastic insulation material. UTP is categorized by the rate of twist; the higher the data rate, the more twists. Cat. 5 has the highest data rate and is the most commonly used for telecom installations.
DEFINITION

UNLICENSED BANDS - Called experimental bands or Garage Bands. As long as FCC rules are not violated, a radio may operate without a license in this band of frequencies. Many telecom service providers exploit this spectrum to provide services. There is even unlicensed PCS (1.920 to 1.930 GHz). Get a PBX, and you can own your own wireless telephone system, without license fees. That's not to say there are no restrictions.

CENSED BANDS - Called experimental bands or Garage Bands. As long as FCC rules are not violated, a radio may operate without a license in this band of frequencies. Many telecom service providers exploit this spectrum to provide services. There is even unlicensed PCS (1.920 to 1.930 GHz). Get a PBX, and you can own your own wireless telephone system, without license fees. That's not to say there are no restrictions.
DEFINITION
V DOT - Jargon for the ITU modem standards. The V dots started being issued when modems first hit the market. V.21 fax is the 300 bits per second facsimile standard.
DEFINITION

VELOCITY OF LIGHT - Common constant used in telecomm engineering. We tend to round up or down, depending on the scale of measure. 186,000 miles per second, 300,000,000 meters per second, or over 985 million feet per second. Theoretically, a photon (light particle) can move faster than an electron, therefore wireless and fiber optics are inherently faster than copper.
DEFINITION
VIRTUAL - Something that exists in cyber space. Cyber space is a place that exists in a computer simulation.
DEFINITION

X.25 - Recognized standard for packetized data communication. Packet structure, assembly & disassembly, and error correction are the hallmarks of X.25. Packet switching was invented at Rand Corporation in the early 1960s; X.25 was published in 1976...
